results.title: Fix: Unsafe Code Loading from User Input Could Execute Malicious Programs in scrapy/commands/genspider.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 978 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: When the spider-generation command loads a module based on user-supplied input, the system shall prevent that input from causing arbitrary code to be executed.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent user-supplied input used to load a module from causing arbitrary code to be executed.

issues: The requirement is stated for the system as a whole, while the evidence localises the behaviour to the spider-generation command (scrapy/commands/genspider.py); the scope given by the evidence is omitted.
As written the sentence asserts a global guarantee that the evidence does not establish, which also makes it hard to check by observation.
unsupported_claims: the implied system-wide scope of the guarantee
missing_information: the affected functionality identified by the evidence: the spider-generation command
revision_instructions: Scope the obligation to the spider-generation command that the evidence identifies, rather than to the system in general; refer to it as user-facing functionality, not by file path.

iteration_history.candidate: When the spider-generation command loads a module based on user-supplied input, the system shall prevent that input from causing arbitrary code to be executed.

results.title: Fix typing of dynamic `request` attribute on `Failure` with a cast subclass
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 937 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue

iteration_history.candidate: When a spider call fails, the system shall expose the associated request on the propagated failure object while preserving that failure's original error context and traceback.

issues: The evidence describes a static-typing change only: it introduces a subclass used via cast() solely for type checkers and states explicitly that runtime behaviour is unchanged and no new Failure instances are created. It therefore establishes no new required behaviour of the system.

The candidate restates pre-existing incidental behaviour (a request attribute dynamically attached to a failure) that the pull request neither introduces nor modifies, and the preservation of error context and traceback is presented in the evidence as a consequence of not changing anything, not as a guarantee established by this change.
unsupported_claims: the system shall expose the associated request on the propagated failure object (as a behaviour introduced or required by this change)
preserving that failure's original error context and traceback (stated in the evidence only as an unchanged side effect of a typing-only change)
